title: Video–EEG alignment
caption: Grey: full video file; green: aligned stimulus interval used for analysis (363 non-overlapping 4-s windows). Video before the stimulus onset and after the end of the EEG recording is discarded.

title: Power spectra after preprocessing
caption: Median power spectral density across channels for each participant after the authors' preprocessing (30 Hz).

title: ISC over the film
caption: Inter-subject correlation per window for every participant (grey) and the group mean (blue) with a moving average.

title: ISC distribution per participant
caption: Box = interquartile range, line = median, whiskers = 1.5 × IQR, over all windows. Level differences between participants motivate subject-wise median labels.

title: Shot-cut detection
caption: Colour-histogram distance between consecutive frames (5 fps). Values above the robust threshold are detected as cuts; they define the shots used for splitting.

title: Distribution of shot durations
caption: 216 shots detected in the aligned stimulus.

title: ISC by shot duration
caption: Mean ISC for windows in short to long shots (quartiles of the current shot's duration); faint lines are individual participants.

title: Feature groups over the film
caption: Mean z-scored value of each feature group per window (5-window moving average), stacked vertically for readability.

title: Correlation structure of the 170 features
caption: Spearman correlations between all features across windows, ordered by feature group (black lines). Blocks of high correlation show redundancy within groups, e.g. motion and editing features.

title: Effective dimensionality of the features
caption: Cumulative variance explained by principal components of the standardised 170 features.

title: PCA of the windows, coloured by audience ISC
caption: One point per window (170 standardised features; unsupervised). Colour = mean ISC over participants; high-ISC windows (red) do not form a single region of feature space.

title: t-SNE of the windows, coloured by audience ISC
caption: One point per window (170 standardised features; unsupervised). Colour = mean ISC over participants; high-ISC windows (red) do not form a single region of feature space.

title: ISC is highest shortly after shot cuts
caption: ISC as a function of time elapsed since the most recent cut (n = windows per bin). Spearman ρ between group ISC and time since cut = -0.34 (descriptive; windows are autocorrelated).

title: t-SNE of CLIP embeddings, coloured by audience ISC
caption: One point per window (512-D CLIP embedding; 52 principal components explain 90 % of its variance). Windows cluster by scene content; ISC varies within clusters.

title: t-SNE of DINOv2 embeddings, coloured by audience ISC
caption: One point per window (384-D DINOv2 embedding; 38 principal components explain 90 % of its variance). Windows cluster by scene content; ISC varies within clusters.

title: Shot-based chronological split
caption: Each bar is one 4-s window. Dotted lines separate the 10 blocks; within each block shots are assigned in time order to train → validation → test, with buffer windows (grey) at every boundary.

title: Strength of correlated components
caption: Generalised eigenvalues of CorrCA fitted on training windows; the first components capture the EEG activity most shared across viewers.

title: Scalp map of correlated component 1
caption: Forward model (spatial pattern) of component 1; sign is arbitrary.

title: ISC per component: training vs held-out windows
caption: Mean ISC of each correlated component in the training, validation and test windows. Similar values on held-out windows show that the CorrCA filters generalise beyond the data they were fitted on.

title: Reliability of the audience ISC time course
caption: Correlation across windows between the mean ISC of two random halves of the participants (200 splits). Higher values mean the ISC time course is more consistent across viewers — a more reliable prediction target.

title: Audience ISC over the film: channel average vs CorrCA
caption: Correlation between the two time courses: r = 0.67.

title: Both ISC measures peak after cuts
caption: Mean (± SEM over viewers) of z-scored ISC by time since the last cut, for channel-average and CorrCA ISC.
